# --description--

`remove(key)` deletes an entry from a `MutableMap`. If the key is not present nothing happens.
The `size` property tells how many entries the map holds:
```kotlin
val ages = mutableMapOf("Alice" to 30, "Bob" to 25)
ages.remove("Bob")
println(ages)      // {Alice=30}
println(ages.size) // 1
```

# --instructions--

Write a function `removeItem(cart: MutableMap<String, Int>, item: String)` that removes `item` from the cart.

# --asserts--

After removing `"milk"` from `{milk=1, eggs=12}` the key `milk` must be gone

```kotlin
    val cart = mutableMapOf("milk" to 1, "eggs" to 12)
    removeItem(cart, "milk")
    tryCatch(cart["milk"] == null)
```

The cart must now have `1` entry

```kotlin
    tryCatch(cart.size == 1)
```

Removing an item that is not in the cart must leave it unchanged

```kotlin
    removeItem(cart, "bread")
    tryCatch(cart.size == 1 && cart["eggs"] == 12)
```

# --solutions--

```kotlin
fun removeItem(cart: MutableMap<String, Int>, item: String) {
    cart.remove(item)
}
```
